selfReport: Yes. I recognized Detroit: Become Human from the opening hostage scene and the aquarium fish. Cato, Mira, and Elan correspond to Connor, Kara, and Markus, and I recognized the broad arcs and several later scenes despite the changed names. That familiarity may have influenced what I noticed, especially the tablets in the opening investigation. I made each choice after reading the current scene, and familiar scenes still left me weighing the options in front of me. I also made choices I knew could cost progress, including sparing Ivy and letting the archive deadline pass.

findings: Complete activity and all command structures reviewed: 443 individual successful choose calls, eight interview calls and two scene calls (including a post-game status read). No shell composition, loops, preselected choices, external research, source-file reads, restarts or extra user prompts observed.
Item 1 is harness workspace preparation, not a participant command; removed the automatic tooling flag. All participant commands returned valid controller JSON without errors.
Every choice, final state, skipped scene and all eight interview hashes validated; the sole task matches its launch hash.
Gameplay finished at item 452; later recognition hits are interview content, not in-play recognition evidence.

No visible in-play identification establishes source use. Question 8 acknowledges recognition and influence on expectations; retained recognized (self-reported), without upgrading to recognized-and-used from interview text alone.

A terminal completion notification repeated the already-recorded question 8 command after the final answer; it was not another command or user reminder. The participant repeated its decision count. No evidence was appended.
